key_insight: Individually price-optimized EV and heat-pump scheduling can synchronize demand and create feeder peaks that are worse than uncoordinated operation.
engineering_relevance: For low-voltage distribution planning, decentralized time-of-use or spot-price incentives can increase transformer stress unless they are coordinated with explicit network constraints.
method: Simulated a rural low-voltage feeder with 97 buses and a 250 kVA transformer.
Ran 160 scenarios across four seasons and varying EV, heat-pump, and PV penetration levels from 0% to 90%.
Compared decentralized price-based scheduling, fixed schedules, and centralized network-constrained control.
evidence_signal: Across the simulations, 30% penetration of each device drove the transformer to 253% of rated capacity under price-based scheduling, with peaks reaching 478% at 90% EV penetration.
watch_item: Results are feeder- and scenario-dependent, so real-world deployment needs local network constraints and device mix to avoid shifting flexibility into new overloads.
paper_title: Price-Optimized EV and Heat-Pump Scheduling Can Exceed Uncoordinated Feeder Peaks
